27. Now, the case of the prosecution against the accused (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors persons is that deceased Geeta was married to accused Pawan on 07.03.2014.
After marriage, all the accused persons, who are in-laws of the deceased, started harassing her verbally and physically for not bringing the sufficient dowry.
All the accused persons were continuously asking the parents and brother of the deceased to fulfill their demand of Rs. 5 lakhs.
They used to harass the deceased for not fulfilling the aforesaid demand.
As per prosecution, the aforesaid continuous harassment meted out to the deceased by her husband and in-laws ultimately compelled her to commit suicide.
28. To prove the offence u/s. 304B IPC, the prosecution i required to establish some basic ingredients of the offence.
Firstly, it has to be proved that the death of the woman has been caused by burns or bodily injury, or has occurred otherwise than normal circumstances.
Secondly, the unnatural death has occurred within seven years of her marriage.
Lastly, that the deceased was being subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of the husband for or in connection with any demand of dowry, soon before her death.
29. As far as first two ingredients are concerned, there appears to be no dispute.

The prosecution witnesses, including the father namely Karamvir Bansal PW-6, mother Kamla Devi PW-10 and father Chahat Ram Bansal PW-9, all have deposed that the deceased was married to accused Pawan on 07.03.2014 and she died due to hanging on 22.10.2014.

There is no dispute (Judgment) State Vs.
Pawan & Ors upon the date of marriage and the date of the death of the deceased.
Cause of death has been proved by PW17/Dr. Pankaj Malya, who has identified the signatures of Dr. Deepak Chaturvedi on the postmortem report PW-17/A.
As per the postmortem report, cause of the death of the deceased was asphyxia as result of ante-mortem hanging.
Thus, the prosecution has successfully proved that the deceased had died an unnatural death within seven years of her marriage.
30. Now comes the third and most important ingredient of the offence u/s 304B that deceased was being subjected to cruelty and harassment soon before her death.

If the prosecution proves this ingredient, a presumption provided u/s 113(B) of Indian Evidence Act shall come into play in favour of the prosecution and against the accused persons that the death of the deceased was a dowry death.
The burden shall then shift towards the accused persons to rebut the statutory presumption by proving the contrary that the death was not a dowry death.
31. Logically, before entering into the probable repercussions of a particular act, firstly the act itself has to be proved.
The unnatural death, for the offence u/s.304B IPC, must be preceded by immediate cruelty and harassment by the accused and that cruelty must be the reason for the unnatural death.
That requisite cruelty can be a specific instance or a continuous conduct consisting of series of acts or omissions.
In (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors both the cases, the specific instance or the series consisting of multiple acts have to be proved specifically, clearly and coherently.

The general, ambiguous and omnibus allegations without specifying any particular incident and specific role played by each accused individually, shall not be sufficient to prove the requisite cruelty in a criminal case.
In other words, the cruelty which ultimately led to the unnatural death of the victim has to be proved specifically like any other fact.

Some of the Hon'ble High Courts State vs Pawan And Others on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123464740/
6 and even Hon'ble Apex Court of India have also expressed the view that general allegations without any specific role and instance are not sufficient to fasten the criminal liability upon the accused.

32. Some of the relevant judgments where the Hon'ble Higher Courts have given observations upon the effect of general allegations are reproduced as under :
33.

In case titled as Shivendra Raizada and Ors. Vs. State of UP and Ors., the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court has held that "We, therefore, deem it just and legally appropriate to quash the proceedings initiated against the appellants Geeta Mehrotra and Ramji Mehrotra as the FIR does not disclose any material which could be held to be constituting any offence against these two appellants.

sentences.text: Merely by making a general allegation that they were also involved in physical and mental torture of the complainant-respondent No.2 without mentioning even a (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors single incident against them as also the fact as to how they could be motivated to demand dowry when they are only related as brother and sister of the complainant's husband, we are pleased to quash and set aside the criminal proceedings in so far as these appellants are concerned and consequently the order passed by the High Court shall stand overruled.
The appeal accordingly is allowed."

34. Further, in case titled as Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam and Ors. Vs. State of Bihar 2022, SC,
Hon'ble SC of India has held as under:
" Coming to the facts of this case, upon a perusal of the contents of the FIR 01.04.2019, it is revealed that general allegations are levelled against the appellants.
The complainant alleged that 'all accused harassed her mentally and threatened her of terminating her pregnancy'.

sentences.text: Furthermore, no specific and distinct allegations have been made against either of the appellants herein, i.e. none of the appellants have been attributed any specific role in furtherance of the general allegations made against them.
This simply leads to a situation wherein one fails to ascertain the role played by each accused in furtherance of the offence.

The allegations are therefore,
general and omnibus and can at best be said to have been made out on account of small skirmishes.
In So far as husband is concerned, since he has not appealed against the order of the High Court, we have not examined the veracity of allegations (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors made against him.
However, as far as the appellants are concerned, the allegations made against them being general and omnibus, do not warrant prosecution.

"Therefore, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in absence of any specific role attributed to the accused/ appellants, it would be unjust if the appellants are forced to go through the tribulation of a trial, that is general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been highlighted by this Court in varied instances , that a criminal try leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scar upon the accused and such an exercise must therefore, be discouraged."

Similarly in the matter of Neelu Chopra and another Vs. Bharti reported in (2009) 10 SCC 184 while quashing the proceedings against father-in-law and mother-in-law has observed as under:
"9. In order to lodge a proper compliant, mere mention of the sections and the language of those sections is not be all and end of the matter.

sentences.text: What is required to be brought to the notice of the court is the particulars of the offence committed by each and every accused and the role played by each and every accused in committing of that offence.
10. "When we see the complaint, the complaint is (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors sadly vague.
It does not show as to which accused has committed what offence and what is the exact role played by these appellants in the commission of offence.
There could be said something against Rajesh, as the allegations are made against him more precisely but he is no more and has already expired.

Under such circumstances, it would be an abuse of process of law to allow the prosecution to continue against the aged parents of Rajesh, the present appellants herein on the basis of vague and general complaint which is silent about the precise acts of the appellants. "
36.
Now, returning to the facts of the present case.
The present case FIR came to be registered on a complaint Ex. PW6/A, lodged by PW6 Karamvir Bansal, brother of the deceased.

In that complaint,
he had leveled allegations against all the accused persons that on 10.08.2014, he alongwith his parents had gone to the matrimonial home of his sister Geeta on occasion of Raksha Bandhan.
There, at the matrimonial home, accused Pawan (husband of the deceased), Gyan Singh (father of the deceased), Mahendri (mother in law of the deceased) and Maneeksha (sister in law of the deceased)
asked them (the parents and brother of the deceased) to fulfill their demand of Rs.5 lacs.
They further told that if their demand is not fulfilled Pawan would divorce Geeta(deceased).
The parents and brother of the deceased assured them to fulfill their demand after some improvement in their (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors financial condition.
PW6 has further deposed that all the accused persons repeated their demands when they again visited the matrimonial home of deceased Geeta on 21.10.2014.

Chahat Ram Bansal, PW9 (father of the deceased) and Kamla Devi, PW10 (mother of the deceased) have also repeated the same allegations as narrated by PW6.
37.
The aforesaid allegations levelled by PW6, PW9 and PW10 shall not be sufficient to prove the offences against the accused persons.
Reason being, neither any specific instance has been elaborated nor any specific role has been assigned to any of the accused.
All the above witnesses have levelled general and omnibus allegation that 'all the accused persons were demanding dowry from them'.

As has been noted above, mere general and omnibus allegation are not sufficient to prove the offence u/s 498A and 304B IPC.
38.
Further, it is not the demand of dowry which is sufficient to invoke offence U/s. 498A and 304B IPC.
The said demand should be accompanied with the harassment and cruelty.
Here, in this case PW6, PW9 and PW10 have deposed in their respective court statements that the accused persons were demanding an amount of Rs.5 lacs from them.

They have nowhere elaborated any specific instance that the accused persons were harassing the deceased because her parents and brother State vs Pawan And Others on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123464740/
8 were not fulfilling their demand of Rs.5lacs.
This court is of the considered opinion that even if, it is believed that the accused persons had (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors demanded Rs.5 lacs from the brother and parents of the deceased.

The said demand alone shall not be sufficient to fulfill the basic ingredients of offence U/s. 498A and 304B IPC which requires that the demand of dowry must be accompanied with the cruelty and harassment to the victim.

As has been noted above, all the witnesses have stated that the accused persons used to demand Rs.5 lacs from them but they did not elaborate anything about the harassment to the deceased for not meeting the said demand.

Thus,
the demand alone, even if believed to be true, shall not be sufficient to prove the case U/s. 498A and 304B IPC.
39.
Furthermore, the case projected by the prosecution is that the deceased was married to accused Pawan on 07.03.2014.
She committed suicide on 22.10.2014 due to the continuous harassment by her in laws for not fulfilling their demand of Rs.5 lacs.

In case, deceased was subjected to cruelty to such an extent that she could not bear it any more and decided to end her life, in that case, it would have been natural conduct of deceased or her parents to report the matter to police, women Cell or any other authority.

If the deceased could not muster the courage to approach the authorities,
nothing had prevented her parents or brother to complain about the alleged conduct of the accused persons but they also did not lodge any complaint regarding the alleged cruel behaviour or demand of dowry by the accused persons before death of the deceased.
Not reporting of the alleged cruel behaviour shall also go against the case of the prosecution.
(Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors 40.
In nutshell, there is no dispute that deceased was married to accused Pawan on 07.03.2014 and she committed suicide on 22.10.2014.
To prove the alleged cruelty and harassment, prosecution has placed reliance upon the testimony of PW6 Karamvir Bansal, PW9 Chahat Ram Bansal and PW10 Kamla Devi.

In their respective statements, they have just deposed that 'all the accused persons'
used to demand Rs.5 lacs from the parents and brother of the deceased.
They did not elaborate any date, time, place, manner and role of any of accused persons in the alleged cruelty to deceased.
These allegations are completely general and omnibus.
In consider opinion of this court, it would not be safe to convict the accused persons for serious offence U/s. 498A and 304B IPC on such general and ominbus allegations.

Accordingly, all the accused persons are acquitted from the charges of offence punishable U/s. 498A/304B IPC.
41.

One more charge framed in alternate against accused persons is for offence U/s. 306 IPC.
42.

Now, this Court shall proceed to see as to whether material collected during investigation of this case is sufficient to fulfill the basic minimum requirement of the offence of abetment to suicide or not.

43. In case titled as Geo Verghese Vs. The State of Rajasthan, SC 2021, The Hon'ble Apex Court while elaborating the ingredients of offence u/s.306 IPC, has observed as under :

sentences.text: What is required to constitute an alleged abetment of suicide under Section 306 IPC is there must be an allegation of either direct or indirect act of incitement to the commission of offence of suicide and mere allegations of harassment of the deceased by another person would not be sufficient in itself, unless, there are allegations of such actions on the part of the accused which compelled the commission of suicide.

Further, if the person committing suicide is hypersensitive and the allegations attributed to the accused is otherwise not ordinarily expected to induce a similarly situated person to take the extreme step of committing suicide, it would be unsafe to hold the accused guilty of abetment of suicide.

Thus, what is required is an examination of every case on its own facts and circumstances and keeping in consideration the surrounding circumstances as well,
which may have bearing on the alleged action of the accused and the psyche of the deceased".
44.

While dealing with case of abetment of suicide in Gurcharan Singh vs The State Of Punjab, SC 2020, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India again explained the parameters of the offence u/s.306 IPC in the following words :
"13. Section 107 IPC defines "abetment" and in this case, the following part of the section will bear consideration: -
"107. Abetment of a thing - A person abets the doing of a thing, who - First-Instigates any person to do that thing; or **** *

entities.text: Gurcharan Singh vs The State Of Punjab, SC 2020
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
*** Thirdly - Intentionally aids,
by any act or illegal omission, the doing of that thing."

14. The definition quoted above makes it clear that whenever a person instigates or intentionally aids by any act or illegal omission, the doing of a thing, a person can be said to have abetted in doing that thing.
(Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors 15.
As in all crimes, mens rea has to be established.
To prove the offence of abetment, as specified under Sec 107 of the IPC, the state of mind to commit a particular crime must be visible, to determine the culpability.

In order to prove mens rea, there has to be something on record to establish or show that the appellant herein had a guilty mind and in furtherance of that state of mind, abetted the suicide of the deceased.
The ingredient of mens rea cannot be assumed to be ostensibly present but has to be visible and conspicuous.
However, what transpires in the present matter is that both the Trial Court as well as the High Court never examined whether appellant had the mens rea for the crime, he is held to have committed.

The conviction of Appellant by the Trial Court as well as the High Court on the theory that the woman with two young kids might have committed suicide, possibly because of the harassment faced by her in the matrimonial house, is not at all borne out by the evidence in the case.
Testimonies of the PWs do not show that the wife was unhappy because of the appellant and she was forced to take such a step on his account.

The necessary ingredients for the offence under section 306 IPC was considered in the case SS Chheena Vs. Vijay Kumar Mahajan1 where explaining the concept of abetment, Justice Dalveer Bhandari wrote as under:-
"25. Abetment involves a mental process of instigating a person or intentionally aiding a 1 (2010) 12 SCC 190 person in doing of a thing.

entities.text: SS Chheena Vs. Vijay Kumar Mahajan1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Without a positive act on the part of the accused to instigate or aid in committing suicide, conviction cannot be sustained.

The intention of the legislature and the ratio of the cases decided by this Court is clear that in order to convict a person under Section 306 IPC there has to be a clear mens rea to commit the (Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors offence.

It also requires an active act or direct act which led the deceased to commit suicide seeing no option and that act must have been intended to push the deceased into such a position that he committed suicide."

17. While dealing with a case of abetment of suicide in Amalendu Pal alias Jhantu vs. State of West Bengal2, Dr. Justice M.K. Sharma writing for the Division Bench explained the parameters of Section 306 IPC in the following terms:

entities.text: Amalendu Pal alias Jhantu vs. State of West Bengal2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "12. Thus, this Court has consistently taken the view that before holding an accused guilty of an offence under Section 306 IPC, the court must scrupulously examine the facts and circumstances of the case and also assess the evidence adduced before it in order to find out whether the cruelty and harassment meted out to the victim had left the victim with no other alternative but to put an end to her life.

It is also to be borne in mind that in cases of alleged abetment of suicide there must be proof of direct or indirect acts of incitement to the commission of suicide".
45.

After discussing the aforesaid law on the offence of abetment of suicide, it becomes clear that to constitute an offence of abetment to suicide u/s.306 IPC, the prosecution must show through the evidence and material collected during investigation that accused intentionally indulged in an act,
either directly or indirectly which pushed the deceased to take her life.
In other words, there must be some conduct attributed to the accused which left the victim with no other alternative than to end her life.
(Judgment) State Vs. Pawan & Ors

Further, if the victim who has committed the suicide is hyper sensitive and the conduct attributed to the accused is otherwise not ordinarily expected to motivate a person of same social background to go to the extent of taking his own life, it is not appropriate to hold the person liable for the offence u/s.306 IPC.
46.

Here in this case, as has been noted above, only general and omnibus allegations have been levelled against 'all the accused persons' that they used to demand Rs.5 lacs from the parents and brother of the deceased.
It has not been elaborated any where that what was the particular conduct of each accused towards the deceased which could have compelled her to commit suicide.
Merely because the deceased committed suicide within 7 months of her marriage does not lead to any presumption that her in laws were responsible or had abetted the said suicide.

Lastly, that the deceased was being subjected to cruelty or harassment by her husband or any relative of the husband for or in connection with any demand of dowry, soon before her death.
If the prosecution proves this ingredient, a presumption provided u/s 113(B) of Indian Evidence Act shall come into play in favour of the prosecution and against the accused persons that the death of the deceased was a dowry death.
The unnatural death, for the offence u/s.304B IPC, must be preceded by immediate cruelty and harassment by the accused and that cruelty must be the reason for the unnatural death.
That requisite cruelty can be a specific instance or a continuous conduct consisting of series of acts or omissions.
The general, ambiguous and omnibus allegations without specifying any particular incident and specific role played by each accused individually, shall not be sufficient to prove the requisite cruelty in a criminal case.
As has been noted above, mere general and omnibus allegation are not sufficient to prove the offence u/s 498A and 304B IPC.
